title: Hardwood Floor Refinishing Sarasota FL | Sand & Finish
description: Hardwood floor refinishing in Sarasota and Manatee County: dust-controlled sanding, stain and finish for $4.50-$7.00 per sq ft in 2026, done in 3-5 days.
h1: Sand-and-Refinish Hardwood Floors in Sarasota and Manatee County
lede: Hardwood floor refinishing brings a scratched, dull or water-stained wood floor in a Sarasota or Manatee County home back to bare wood and a fresh finish, without tearing anything out.
capsule: Hardwood floor refinishing means sanding an existing wood floor down to bare grain, then restaining and recoating it, instead of replacing the boards. In Sarasota and Manatee County we price sand-and-refinish work at $4.50 to $7.00 per square foot in 2026, using vacuum-shrouded sanders to cut down on dust. Most homes are done in three to five working days, plus finish cure time.

sections.html:
Sand-and-refinish means taking the wood down to bare grain with a drum or orbital sander, then rebuilding the finish from scratch. We start with a coarse grit, usually 36 or 40, to strip old polyurethane and level out scratches, then step through progressively finer grits so the sanding marks disappear before stain goes on. An edger handles the perimeter and any spots the big sander can't reach, and a corner tool gets into closets and under toe-kicks.

Once the boards are bare, we vacuum, tack the floor, and apply stain if the homeowner wants a color change. Plenty of Sarasota houses built before the 1990s have red oak that reads orange under an old amber finish, and a gray or natural stain resets that look without replacing a single board. Two to three coats of polyurethane follow, with a light scuff sand between coats for adhesion. We also install new solid and engineered hardwood flooring, so matching a refinished floor to a new one in an adjoining room draws on the same crew and the same stain formulas. Most of the solid floors we refinish in older Sarasota neighborhoods are red or white oak, with the occasional heart pine turning up in a pre-1960s cottage; each species takes stain a little differently, which is why we sand a test patch in a closet before committing to a color for the whole room.

Dust-controlled refinishing hooks the drum sander, edger and buffer to a vacuum with a HEPA-rated filter, so most of the wood dust gets pulled into a canister instead of settling on furniture, baseboards and the lanai next door. We tape off doorways and run a portable air scrubber in the work zone on multi-day jobs. That cuts dust noticeably compared with an open sander, but it doesn't eliminate it. Fine dust still escapes right at the point of contact and settles in the work area for a day or two, so we cover cabinet hardware and close vents into the rest of the house before starting. A central-air return near the work zone gets a temporary filter over it too, so the system isn't pulling fine sanding dust through the ductwork and back out in every other room.

Homeowners searching for dustless hardwood floor refinishing near me are usually trying to avoid the old shop-vac-and-open-sander approach that used to coat an entire house in fine oak dust. Vacuum-shrouded sanding gets close to that without promising a dust-free house on day one.

sections.h2: What does hardwood floor refinishing cost in Sarasota in 2026?
sections.html:
Hardwood floor refinishing in Sarasota and Manatee County typically runs $4.50 to $7.00 per square foot installed in 2026, covering sanding, stain and two to three coats of polyurethane on a floor that's already down. A 300-square-foot living and dining area lands around $1,350 to $2,100 before any board replacement or water-damage repair. That's a typical range, not a quote, so run your own square footage through the flooring cost calculator or ask at the free estimate.

National figures point the same direction: HomeGuide (2026) puts refinishing at $2 to $8 per square foot, $800 to $3,200 for a typical job, and Angi's 2026 data averages around $1,891 with dustless refinishing running $5 to $8 per square foot. Our dust-controlled process sits inside that band already, without a separate dustless upcharge. The hardwood flooring cost guide compares refinishing against a full tear-out and new install.

sections.h2: How long does a refinish take?
sections.html:
A full sand-and-refinish runs three to five working days for an average home: a day or two of sanding, staining if needed, and two to three coats of polyurethane with dry time between coats. Water-based polyurethane is walkable in socks within about 24 hours and lets furniture back in after a few days. Oil-based poly looks warmer on red and white oak but needs up to 30 days to fully cure before rugs or furniture pads go back down, so plan around that if the job lands before a rental turnover or a family visit.

Sarasota's wet season adds a wrinkle: high humidity slows dry time between coats, so a refinish booked in July or August often needs an extra day compared with the same job in February. If part of the project involves boards damaged by water or termites, ask about floor repair first — you can't sand a rotted board back to good wood, it has to come out and be replaced before sanding starts.

sections.h2: How many times can a floor be refinished?
sections.html:
Solid hardwood, the 3/4-inch boards common in Sarasota's older block homes, can typically take about four full sandings over its life, sometimes up to ten light screen-and-recoat passes that skip a full sand. Engineered hardwood has a thin wood layer glued over a plywood core, so how many times it can be refinished depends on that layer's thickness: a 2 mm wear layer allows roughly one to two sandings, 3 mm allows two to three, and 4 mm allows three to four, since a full sanding removes about 0.5 to 1 mm of wood each time.

If you're not sure which you have, check a floor vent or a spot where a board has already been swapped out. Solid wood is the same species all the way through; engineered shows a thin veneer over a different-colored core. We cover that difference, including gluing engineered boards directly to a slab, on the engineered hardwood flooring page.

Water-based polyurethane dries faster, stays clear instead of ambering over the years, and has less odor during application, which matters in a closed-up Florida house where central air recirculates the same indoor air all day. Oil-based polyurethane costs less per gallon, lays down a warmer amber tone that a lot of owners of older red oak floors still prefer, and holds up marginally better under heavy furniture traffic, but it takes longer to cure and smells stronger while it does. Satin and matte sheens hide dust and light scratches better than semi-gloss, which is part of why most of the homes we refinish end up somewhere in the satin-to-matte range instead of a mirror finish.

For a rental or a house with dogs, we usually steer owners toward a water-based finish with a higher solids content, since it recoats faster between guest turnovers and doesn't leave the unit smelling of solvent for renters arriving a day or two later. For a primary residence that won't see heavy wear, oil-based still has a following for its color and its long track record as the standard finish.

sections.h2: Refinish or replace, and getting the house ready
sections.html:
Refinishing only works if the wood itself is sound. A floor that's cupping, with boards curling up at the edges, usually means moisture is reaching the wood from below or from a leak, and sanding it before that source is fixed causes a worse problem called crowning once the wood dries back out. We check with a moisture meter first. Mild cupping often flattens on its own over a few weeks to months once the humidity source is corrected, and only then does sanding make sense; our take on when replacement beats a refinish goes through the rest of that call.

Getting ready for the crew means clearing the room of furniture and rugs (we move light items; heavier pieces are on the homeowner) and boarding pets elsewhere for the sanding days, since the noise and dust make a house uncomfortable for cats and dogs no matter how well the vacuum shrouds work. A 1970s block ranch in Gulf Gate with original oak underneath decades of carpet is a common example: once the carpet and tack strips come out, the floor is often refinishable rather than a full replacement, which saves the homeowner thousands. Refinishing pays back well at resale, too: the 2022 NAR/NARI Remodeling Impact Report found it recovered about 147% of its cost, ahead of installing new wood flooring at 118%. It's covered by the same two-year workmanship warranty as a new install — ask about scheduling at the free estimate.

faqs.q: How much does hardwood floor refinishing cost in Sarasota?
faqs.a: Sand-and-refinish work runs $4.50 to $7.00 per square foot installed in 2026 in Sarasota and Manatee County, covering sanding, stain and two to three coats of finish. A 300 sq ft room typically falls between $1,350 and $2,100; get an exact number at your free estimate.

faqs.q: How long does hardwood floor refinishing take?
faqs.a: Most homes take three to five working days for sanding, staining and two to three coats of finish. Water-based polyurethane is walkable in about 24 hours; oil-based needs up to 30 days to fully cure before rugs go back down.

No. Vacuum-shrouded sanders and an air scrubber capture most of the wood dust at the source, cutting down significantly on what settles on furniture and baseboards, but fine dust still escapes and the work area needs a wipe-down afterward.

faqs.q: Can engineered hardwood be refinished the same way?
faqs.a: It depends on the wear layer. A 2 mm wear layer allows about one to two sandings, 3 mm allows two to three, and 4 mm allows three to four, since each full sanding removes roughly 0.5 to 1 mm of wood.

faqs.q: What if the floor is cupping instead of just dull?
faqs.a: Cupped boards usually mean moisture is reaching the wood from below or from a leak. Sanding before that source is fixed causes crowning once the wood dries out, so we check with a moisture meter and wait for readings to normalize first.

faqs.q: Do we need to leave the house during refinishing?
faqs.a: Most people stay, but pets do better elsewhere for the sanding days, and rooms next to the work zone should stay closed off. Strong odor from oil-based polyurethane is the main reason some households choose to be out for a night or two.

faqs.q: Does refinishing hardwood floors increase home value?
faqs.a: The 2022 NAR/NARI Remodeling Impact Report found hardwood refinishing recovered about 147% of its cost on average, more than installing new wood flooring at 118%, making it one of the better-returning projects in that report.
